newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Government warns rebels not to restart Angolan war.
newsitem.headline: Government warns rebels not to restart Angolan war.

text.p: The Angolan government on Friday said the former rebel movement UNITA was gathering soldiers and war material, posing a threat to the peace accord that ended the 20-year Angolan civil war in 1994.

In its first official statement on a three-week-old flareup of fighting between the two sides in the north, the government said UNITA's actions "could put in danger the Lusaka protocols, with all the grave consequences that would entail".
"UNITA is gathering men and war materiel and its actions are not helping Angola's peace process," the statement said. "The United Nations must adopt measures to stop these belligerent intentions."
"The government has no intentions of returning to war...the government cannot ignore its own responsibilities to secure the frontier," it added.

A political analyst who declined to be named said UNITA was bringing in arms from Sofia, Bulgaria, to its Andula stronghold in DC-10 aircraft, after extending the landing strip there to accommodate the planes.

The fighting in the north began three weeks ago when the government ordered the army to advance into diamond-rich territory held by UNITA, which had just lost its main African ally, ex-Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko, who was toppled in a revolt backed by Luanda.
